title: Henselian lifts of prescribed models on a finite closed covering
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation for derived tensor with unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, satisfying both triangle identities. Put $L_T(P)=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ for the canonical scalar realization [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization], where underlines are discrete constant sheaves. A perfect ring complex is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $I_a\subseteq A$ be ideals indexed by a finite set, with $X_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_a)$ whose underlying closed subsets cover $X$. Let $K\in D(X,\Lambda)$ be dualizable. For each $a$, suppose given an affine faithfully flat ind-etale cover $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C_a\to X_a$ with $W_a$ w-contractible [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, sk-def-pe-wlocal], a perfect $P_a\in D(R)$, and a derived isomorphism $\alpha_a:K|_{W_a}\simeq L_{W_a}(P_a)$.

Set $C_a=H_A(\overline C_a)$ using the small filtered-diagram colimit construction [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], and put $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$. Then $C_a$ is ind-etale over $A$, its specified reduction map $C_a/I_aC_a\to\overline C_a$ is an isomorphism, the pair $(C_a,I_aC_a)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and $V_a$ is w-contractible. Under this identification of the closed fiber with $W_a$, there is a unique derived isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha_a:K|_{V_a}\simeq L_{V_a}(P_a)$ restricting to $\alpha_a$.

Each $V_a\to X$ is weakly etale and its image contains $|X_a|$. The finite affine disjoint union $\coprod_a V_a\to X$ is surjective, flat and quasi-compact, and the family $\{V_a\to X\}_a$ is a pro-etale covering. The $P_a$ need not agree. The statement includes the empty index set when $X$ is empty; it does not assert that arbitrary closed subschemes of w-contractible schemes are w-contractible.

source.place: Theorem 4.13, finite-component paragraph refined by w-contractible covers; Corollary 4.4(2); Bhatt--Scholze Definition 2.2.10 and Lemmas 2.2.12, 6.1.1

proof.text: Fix an index $a$ and abbreviate $I=I_a$, $\overline C=\overline C_a$, $C=H_A(\overline C)$ and $J=IC$. The indexing category in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift] is small, and is filtered by [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered]. Its terms are finitely presented etale $A$-algebras, so its colimit $C$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The specified map $C/J\to\overline C$ is an isomorphism by [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction], and $(C,J)$ is henselian by [lem-zl-henselian-indetale-closed-lift].

source.place: Definition 2.2.10, Lemma 2.2.12, and the henselian assertion in the proof of Lemma 6.1.2; Stacks Tag 097P (lemma-lift-ind-etale)

proof.text: Use the bijective specified reduction to form a ring equivalence C/J ≃ Cbar. Transport w-contractibility across this equivalence (the proved private RingHom.wContractible_of_ringEquiv helper in WeilConjectures.RingTheory.WContractibleGeometricCriterion). Apply [lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity] to (C,J): C is w-contractible, and quotient pullback is fully faithful on dualizable objects. The specified fiber map is the quotient immersion preceded by the spectrum isomorphism of the reduction equivalence. Pullback along that isomorphism is an equivalence: derive upperStarComp and upperStarId to exhibit its inverse. Therefore the actual specified fiber pullback is fully faithful on dualizable objects.

By [lem-zl-condensed-lisse-proetale-locality], inverse image along $V_a\to X$ preserves dualizability, so $K|_{V_a}$ is dualizable. Since $P_a$ is perfect and $V_a$ is w-contractible affine, [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-projective-calculus] makes $L_{V_a}(P_a)$ dualizable. The same inverse-image lemma gives the canonical identification $i_a^*L_{V_a}(P_a)\simeq L_{W_a}(P_a)$. Thus $\alpha_a$ is an isomorphism between the restrictions of these two dualizable objects.

source.place: Section 3 pullback paragraph; Lemma 4.1; Theorem 4.13, reverse implication and finite-component paragraph

proof.text: Let M be K pulled back to Spec C and N the prescribed scalar realization of P. Regard M and N as objects of the full subcategory of dualizable objects, using step 3. Compose the fully faithful quotient pullback of [lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity] with the inclusion and the equivalence from the reduction isomorphism in step 2. Transport the given alpha by the inverse derived-composition comparison and inverse canonical scalar comparison. Mathlib Functor.FullyFaithful.isoEquiv gives its unique preimage isomorphism M ≅ N. Cancellation of those two specified comparisons proves that its restriction is exactly alpha. The same cancellation and injectivity prove uniqueness.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(2); the unique extension in Theorem 4.13, finite-component paragraph

proof.text: The already proved source instance Algebra.IndEtale.weaklyEtale (WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.IndWeaklyEtale), specialized to ClosedLift, makes each structure morphism weakly etale and hence flat [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. The given faithfully flat map A/I_a → Cbar_a is surjective on spectra by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Composing its preimages with the retained fiber map proves the asserted range inclusion, since the retained map is an A-algebra homomorphism and the A-algebra structure on Cbar factors through A/I_a. The range of Spec(A/I_a) → Spec A is the zero locus of I_a. The covering hypothesis therefore gives joint surjectivity of the lifted family.

The finite coproduct of the affine schemes Spec C_a is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Its map to Spec A is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence quasi-compact. Joint surjectivity from step 5 gives surjectivity of Sigma.desc. Flatness is local on the open summands: apply Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc to their flat structure morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism].

Package the finite family as a PreZeroHypercover. Each structure map is quasi-compact because it is a morphism of affine schemes [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. For an affine open U, each member is spectral and the family is jointly surjective. Mathlib IsCompactOpenCovered.of_finite_of_isSpectralMap therefore gives the QuasiCompactCover condition. Together with joint surjectivity and weak etaleness this is precisely [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. All APIs allow a finite index in a separate universe, including the empty index type. No step compares different P_a or assumes that arbitrary closed subschemes of w-contractible schemes are w-contractible.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 4.13 finite-component paragraph, refined to prescribed w-contractible covers instead of assuming arbitrary closed subschemes are w-contractible; Corollary 4.4(2); Bhatt--Scholze Definition 2.2.10 and Lemmas 2.2.12, 6.1.1. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q68-8dbc82de9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole split; I make no changes. The item's statement matches live byte for byte, and live still has the item unsplit with no repair note, so no re-split rule applies. The stmt_deps edit is fine: def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor is dropped (its use already goes through def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization), and the weakly étale, flat, finite-type/quasi-compact and pro-étale-covering definitions the last paragraph uses are added. Source: I read HRS (arXiv 2305.18131) Cor 4.4(1)(2) and the finite-component paragraph of Thm 4.13 in the local PDF. The item swaps the BS 2.2.15 closed-subscheme shortcut for the given w-contractible covers W_a, and uses the ind-étale lift H_A instead of the henselization. Steps: 1 (filtered small diagram ⇒ ind-étale; reduction C/IC≅C̄; henselian pair) uses exactly what the cited statements say. 2: the rigidity node gives V_a w-contractible, since w-contractibility is an iso-invariant ring property and Spec(C/IC)≅W_a, and gives i^* fully faithful on dualizable objects. 3: locality says f^* keeps dualizables and commutes with L(P); the projective calculus makes L_V(P) dualizable without flatness. The equality W_a→V_a→X = W_a→X_a→X holds because ε is an A-algebra map. 4: lifting α and α⁻¹ and uniqueness are elementary. 5: ind-étale ⇒ weakly étale ⇒ flat; faithfully flat ⇒ surjective on spectra; with the factorisation this gives joint surjectivity. 6: permanence clauses (3),(4), morphisms of affines are affine, flatness on local rings. 7: definition of fpqc/pro-étale covering. Edge cases checked: empty index set (X=∅), I_a=A (C̄=0 is terminal, so C=0), I_a=0, distinct P_a, nonreduced A, non-f.g. ideals. No new nodes, no cycle, no SGA. Batch-5 flag: rigidity → wstrict-local-invariance → lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting, which is Stacks 0H74 (smooth algebra maps lift along henselian pairs). That is pure commutative algebra, given by neither the trace-formula leaf nor the Poincaré-duality leaf and not a step of either, so I accept it. I accept the split_report tool_uses (closed-lift construction and lemmas from sk-prop-sf-open-closed-triangle, plus generic pbc ind-étale, flat, affine and covering tools); for the maintainer: the worker wrote tool_uses themselves, against C8.

lean.note: Uses the actual small filtered-colimit Algebra.ClosedLift and its retained map. The input restriction to W_a is written along closedModelFiberMap followed by closedModelLiftMap, which is its given A-structure morphism because toAlgHom is an A-algebra map. closedModelRestriction uses the canonical derived composition and scalar-realization comparisons, so the unique isomorphism restricts to the prescribed alpha_a.
